sections.heading: Features of literary Spanish
sections.body:
Literary texts use things you rarely hear in conversation:

- **The -ra form as pluperfect indicative** (from Latin): *el hombre que conociera en su juventud* = *que había conocido* (the man she had met in her youth). Common in journalism too.
- **Enclitic pronouns on conjugated verbs** (old-fashioned / literary): *Díjole que se fuera* = *Le dijo…* *Érase una vez…* (Once upon a time…)
- **Word order inversion**: *Grande fue su sorpresa.* (Great was his surprise.)
- **The preterite anterior** (*hube + participle*, after *apenas, cuando, en cuanto*): *Apenas hubo terminado, salió.* (No sooner had he finished than he left.)
- **Rich imagery and figurative language**: *metáfora, símil (como…), personificación, hipérbole*.

sections.heading: The future subjunctive
sections.body:
The future subjunctive (*-re*: *hablare, comiere, fuere, hubiere*) disappeared from speech centuries ago but survives in **legal texts** and **set phrases**:

- Law: *El que infringiere esta norma será sancionado.* (Whoever infringes this rule shall be penalized.) *Si no hubiere acuerdo…* (Should there be no agreement…)
- Proverbs and phrases: *Adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres.* (When in Rome, do as the Romans do.) *Sea lo que fuere* (whatever it may be), *venga lo que viniere*.

You only need to **recognise** it: form it from the *ellos* preterite (*hablaron → hablare*), like the imperfect subjunctive but with *-re*.

sections.heading: Great names to read
sections.body: Short and accessible first: Julio Cortázar's short stories (*Casa tomada*), Jorge Luis Borges (*Ficciones*), Juan Rulfo (*Pedro Páramo*), Gabriel García Márquez (*Crónica de una muerte anunciada*), Isabel Allende, Laura Esquivel (*Como agua para chocolate*), Mario Benedetti's poems, Pablo Neruda (*Veinte poemas de amor*), Gabriela Mistral, Samanta Schweblin and Mariana Enríquez for contemporary fiction.

examples: Érase una vez un rey muy triste.
Once upon a time there was a very sad king.
Volvió a ver al hombre que conociera en su juventud.
She saw again the man she had met in her youth.
Grande fue su sorpresa al abrir la puerta.
Great was his surprise on opening the door.
Apenas hubo terminado, salió de la sala.
No sooner had he finished than he left the room.
Sus ojos eran dos luceros.
Her eyes were two bright stars.
Era fuerte como un roble.
He was as strong as an oak.
Te lo he dicho un millón de veces.
I've told you a million times.
El narrador cuenta la historia desde el futuro.
The narrator tells the story from the future.
El que infringiere esta norma será sancionado.
Whoever infringes this rule shall be penalized.
Si no hubiere acuerdo, decidirá el juez.
Should there be no agreement, the judge will decide.
Adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres.
When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
Sea lo que fuere, hay que seguir adelante.
Whatever it may be, we have to carry on.
Pedro Páramo es una novela de Juan Rulfo.
Pedro Páramo is a novel by Juan Rulfo.
Casa tomada es un cuento de Cortázar.
House Taken Over is a short story by Cortázar.
